sentences.text:
For ready reference, the same is reproduced hereinunder:-
"Heard Mr. Dileep Kumar Yadav, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State and Mrs. Gunjan Sharma, the learned counsel representing opposite party-3.

This application for bail has been filed by applicant-Simraan seeking his enlargement on bail in Case Crime No.121 of 2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376, 313, 120-B IPC and Section 3/4 Pocso Act, police station South, district Firozabad, during the pendency of trial.
Perused the record.
At the very outset, learned A.G.A. submits that notice of the present application for bail has been served upon first informant-opposite party-4 on 17.07.2023.

However,
in spite of service of notice, no one has put in appearance on behalf of first informant-opposite party-4 to oppose this application for bail.

Record shows that in respect of an incident which is alleged to have occurred on 25.03.2021, a delayed F.I.R. dated 27.02.2023 was lodged by first informant, namely,
Smt. Bushra (mother of the prosecutrix) and was registered as Case Crime No.0121 of 2023, under Sections 363, 376, 313, 120-B IPC and Section 3/4 Pocso Act, police station South, district Firozabad.

In the aforesaid F.I.R., five persons, namely,
Simraan; Nisar Ali; Sahil; Smt. Guddi and Dr. Ragini Agrawal have been nominated as named accused.
Learned counsel for the applicant contends that though applicant is a named and charge-sheeted accused, yet he is liable to be enlarged on bail.

The occurrence giving rise to the present criminal proceedings is alleged to have occurred on 25.03.2021,
whereas the F.I.R. was lodged on 27.02.2023.
As such, there is a delay of almost two years in lodging the F.I.R.

Since the delay in lodging the F.I.R. has not been sufficiently explained either in the F.I.R. or in the statement of first informant recorded under Section 161 CrPC therefore, by virtue of the law laid down by the Apex Court in P. Rajagopal Vs. The State of Tamil Nadu AIR 2019 SC 2866 (paragraph 8), the criminal proceedings itself cannot be maintained against the applicant.

entities.text: P. Rajagopal Vs. The State of Tamil Nadu AIR 2019 SC 2866
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is then contended by the learned counsel for applicant that it is an admitted case of the prosecution as unfolded in the F.I.R. itself that the prosecutrix has solemnized Simraan vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152454655/
2 marriage (Nikah) with the applicant.
In view of above, the criminality alleged against the applicant cannot be said to have been committed by him.

The police report under Section 173(2) CrPC has already been submitted against four of the named accused including applicant on 02.04.2023, whereas one of the named accused, namely, Dr. Ragini Agrawal has been exculpated.
As such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystalized.
Up to this stage, no such circumstance has emerged necessitating the custodial arrest of the applicant.
Even otherwise, the applicant is a man of clean antecedents having no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
The applicant is in jail since 18.03.2023, as such he has undergone six months of incarceration.
He, therefore, submits that the applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.

He submits that in compliance of the order dated 07.08.2023 passed by this Court,
Investigating Officer has collected some material in consonance with the provisions contained in Section 94 of The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act,
2015.

sentences.text: The said material has been brought on record by means of compliance affidavit filed by learned A.G.A. in Court today.

Attention of the Court was then invited to the certificate issued by the Principal, Composite Vidyalaya, Nagla Kirat, City area,
Mainpuri.
As per the said certificate issued by the Principal of said institution, the date of birth of the prosecutrix as recorded in the school record is 16.05.2005.
The occurrence giving rise to the present criminal proceeding occurred on 25.03.2021.
As such, the prosecutrix was aged about 16 years 02 months and 20 days on the date of occurrence.

Attention of the Court was invited to the application filed by first informant before the Station House Office/Inspector, police station South, district Firozabad, wherein it has categorically been stated that certificate which has been issued by the Principal of the institution, copy of which has been brought on record as Annexure-CA-1 of compliance affidavit, is the same institution which was first attended by the prosecutrix.
On the above premise, the learned A.G.A. submits that the prosecutrix was a young girl of tender age on the date of occurrence.

According to the learned A.G.A. though there is a recital in the F.I.R. that forcibly marriage (Nikah) was solemnized by the applicant with the prosecutrix but the applicant himself has failed to bring on record any document that marriage (Nikah) was got solemnized between the parties.

With regard to the delay in lodging of the F.IR., the learned A.G.A. invited the attention of the Court to the F.I.R. itself and on basis of recital contained therein he submits that the delay in lodging the F.I.R. has been duly explained.
On the above premise, he submits that the applicant does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.
The applicant is guilty of dislodging the modesty of the prosecutrix repeatedly and continuously who was admittedly below 18 years of age on the date of occurrence.
As such, no sympathy be shown by this court in favour of the applicant.

The offence complained of is not private in nature but a crime against Simraan vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152454655/
3 society.
In fact, the crime committed by applicant falls in the category of moral turpitude.
As such, no good ground has been made out to enlarge the applicant on bail.
When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.

Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of material brought on record, nature and gravity of offence, evidence,
complicity of the accused, accusation made coupled with the fact that there is nothing on record on the basis of which the credibility or reliability of the prosecutrix could be doubted, the statements of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161/164 CrPC clearly establish the complicity of the applicant in the crime in question, no such material has been brought on record on the basis of which it can be inferred that the prosecution of the applicant is false or malicious, the submissions urged by the learned A.G.A. in opposition to the present application for bail could not be dislodged by the learned counsel for applicant with reference to the record at this stage therefore irrespective of the submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant in support of the bail application but, without making any comment on the merits of the case, this Court does not find any good ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
This application for bail thus fails and is liable to be rejected.

It is accordingly rejected."
6.
Learned counsel for applicant contends that subsequent to the order dated 18.09.2023 the trial of applicant commenced before court below by way of aforementioned trial.

The first informant Busra,
(mother of the prosecutrix) deposed before court below as PW 1, whereas the prosecutrix deposed before court below as PW2.
While first informant PW1 has supported the F.I.R. but the prosecurix in her deposition before court below has not supported the F.I.R.
On the above premise, the learned counsel for applicant contends that once the prosecutrix has herself not supported the F.I.R., no good ground exists to prolong the custodial arrest of applicant.
He therefore, contends that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.

It is next contended that since the statement of the first informant and prosecutrix have been recorded, therefore, in case, the applicant is enlarged on bail,
then it cannot be said that applicant shall either terrorize the witnesses or shall hamper the course of trial.
7.
Even otherwise, applicant is a man of clean antecedents inasmuch as, he has no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is in jail since 19.03.2023.
As such, he has undergone more than 11 months of incarceration.
The police report in terms of Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted on 02.04.2023.
As such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallized.
However, upto this stage, no such incriminating circumstance has emerged on record necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial.

To butteress his submission, he has relied upon the judgment of the Supreme Simraan vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152454655/

In case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and shall co-operate with the trial.
8. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail.
He submits that since applicant is a named and charge sheeted accused, therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.
The mother of the prosecutrix who has deposed before court below as PW1 and has fully supported the F.I.R.
As such, no indulgence be granted by this Court in favour of applicant.
However, the learned A.G.A. could not dislodge the factual and legal submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant with reference to the record at this stage.

9. Having heard, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of record, evidence, complicity of applicant, gravity and nature of offence and accusation made coupled with the fact that prosecutrix in her deposition before court below as PW 2 has not supported the F.I.R., once the prosecutrix has herself not supported the F.I.R., no good ground exists to prolong the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial, the clean antecedents of the applicant,
the period of incarceration undergone and inspite of the fact that the charge sheet has been submitted, therefore, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution stands crystallized yet inspite of above, learned A.G.A. could not point out any such circumstance from the record necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial, the judgment of Supreme Court in Sumit Subhaschandra Gangwal (Supra), since, the statement of the first informant and the prosecutrix have already recorded before court below, therefore, in case, the applicant is enlarged on bail, then it cannot be said that in case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall either terrorize the witnesses or shall hamper the course of trial, therefore, irrespective of the objections raised by the learned A.G.A. in opposition to this repeat application for bail, but without making any comment on the merits of the case, applicant has made out a case for bail.
10.
Accordingly, the bail application is Allowed.

11. Let the applicant-Simraan, be released on bail in aforesaid case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) THE APPLICANT SHALL FILE AN UNDERTAKING TO THE EFFECT THAT HE/SHE SHALL NOT SEEK ANY ADJOURNMENT ON THE DATE FIXED FOR EVIDENCE WHEN THE WITNESSES ARE PRESENT IN COURT.
IN CASE OF DEFAULT OF THIS CONDITION, IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT IT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PASS ORDERS IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.
(ii) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON EACH DATE FIXED, EITHER PERSONALLY OR THROUGH HIS/HER COUNSEL.

IN CASE OF HIS/HER ABSENCE, WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THE TRIAL Simraan vs State Of U.P. on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152454655/
5 COURT MAY PROCEED AGAINST HIM/HER UNDER SECTION 229-A IPC.

entities.text: TRIAL Simraan vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(iii) IN CASE, THE APPLICANT MISUSES THE LIBERTY OF BAIL DURING TRIAL AND IN ORDER TO SECURE HIS/HER PRESENCE PROCLAMATION UNDER SECTION 82 CR.P.C., MAY BE ISSUED AND IF APPLICANT FAILS TO APPEAR BEFORE THE COURT ON THE DATE FIXED IN SUCH PROCLAMATION, THEN,
THE TRIAL COURT SHALL INITIATE PROCEEDINGS AGAINST HIM/HER, IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW, UNDER SECTION 174-A IPC.

(iv) THE APPLICANT SHALL REMAIN PRESENT, IN PERSON, BEFORE THE TRIAL COURT ON DATES FIXED FOR (1) OPENING OF THE CASE, (2) FRAMING OF CHARGE AND (3) RECORDING OF STATEMENT UNDER SECTION 313 CR.P.C. IF IN THE OPINION OF THE TRIAL COURT ABSENCE OF THE APPLICANT IS DELIBERATE OR WITHOUT SUFFICIENT CAUSE, THEN IT SHALL BE OPEN FOR THE TRIAL COURT TO TREAT SUCH DEFAULT AS ABUSE OF LIBERTY OF BAIL AND PROCEED AGAINST THE HIM/HER IN ACCORDANCE WITH LAW.

(v) THE TRIAL COURT MAY MAKE ALL POSSIBLE EFFORTS/ENDEAVOUR AND TRY TO CONCLUDE THE TRIAL WITHIN A PERIOD OF ONE YEAR AFTER THE RELEASE OF THE APPLICANT.
12.

However, it is made clear that any wilful violation of above conditions by the applicant, shall have serious repercussion on his/her bail so granted by this Court and the trial court is at liberty to cancel the bail, after recording the reasons for doing so, in the given case of any of the condition mentioned above.
